adversarial_audit.objection: The filter secretly pays the direct physical-to-Gram success factor.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Its operations are physical isotypic measurement and branch-register interference; no T^* map or label-index postselection appears.

adversarial_audit.objection: A noncovariant branch filter can fail on most hidden labels.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Uniform conjugation makes acceptance exactly constant over the orbit in every finite control.

adversarial_audit.objection: Exact common-core rejection proves a polynomial postfilter norm.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Near-common directions and obstruction families not aligned with the chosen H may remain.

adversarial_audit.objection: High retained trace proves hidden-label mutual information is retained.
adversarial_audit.resolution: A filter can retain average mass while erasing the label-dependent component. The postfilter ensemble needs an explicit information or decoding theorem.

claim_gate.reason: A polynomial direct physical common-core filter now exists, and its natural information retention is proved. The residual filtered-frame spectrum and decoder are unproved.

falsifiers_triggered: The factorial direct physical-to-Gram access obstruction is not an obstruction to branch-register interference.
Selected orientation common cores can be rejected directly and covariantly at unit scale.
No speedup follows until retained information, residual norm, outcome measurement, decoding, and classical separation close.

proof_obligations.resolution: A known rectangular flip identifies both induced summands with V_lambda tensor V_mu and turns the base bridge into X.
Diagonal S_n isotypic measurement, a GF(2) basis change, and Hadamards implement the filter on the physical carrier.
Fourier Parseval inside each orientation coset gives the recorded d_nu |H|/2^k weighted sum of Tr(F_q-F_q^2).
Uniformly conjugating the filter equalizes hidden-label acceptance while retaining the random conjugator for decoding.
No natural Plancherel theorem yet bounds the weighted coset second moments or the filtered frame norm after composing enough subspaces to remove every obstruction.

summary: Lifted orientation-character interference from the dual Gram description to a direct polynomial physical-carrier circuit and proved its exact coset trace-transfer identity; the companion Plancherel theorem proves typical information retention.

theorem_contract.access_model: The circuit acts directly on physical branch carriers and does not use the synthesis adjoint T^*.
theorem_contract.common_core_rejection: A vector common to all E_nu,q+h in a coset is an eigenvalue-one vector of F_nu,q and contributes zero after filtering.
theorem_contract.complexity: Branch alignment and GF(2) transforms use poly(k) gates; diagonal S_n isotypic measurement is polynomial via the symmetric-group QFT.
theorem_contract.covariantization: Uniform random diagonal conjugation makes conclusive probability independent of the hidden permutation.
theorem_contract.filter: Measure diagonal isotypic nu, Fourier transform a selected orientation subspace H within every quotient coset, and accept nontrivial H character.
theorem_contract.physical_carrier: After known branch flips, unequal k-copy carriers have an explicit F_2^k orientation register.
